title: What does LedgerStateFix do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of LedgerStateFix and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, LedgerStateFix repairs specified ledger-state inconsistencies under a supported repair amendment. [1]

The reference defines a repair type and affected owner rather than authorizing arbitrary edits to balances. This is maintenance for recognized state problems, not a normal payment or a general database administrator command. Check the required amendment and exact repair scope. A successful repair should be reported with its validated result and the affected ledger object. [1]

The LedgerStateFix reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using LedgerStateFix, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
